claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

First, could you please tell me how many children you're looking to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names and ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text:
Hello! Yes, I'm interested in claiming Child Benefit and wondering if I'm eligible.

I have one child - Alex, who is 18 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information about Alex.

Since Alex is 18 years old, their eligibility for Child Benefit depends on their current situation. You can normally still qualify for Child Benefit if your child is under 20 and stays in approved education or training.

Could you please tell me, is Alex currently in any of the following:
- Full-time non-advanced education (such as A-levels, Scottish Highers, or equivalent)
- Approved training (not paid for by an employer)

Or has Alex left education/training, or started work?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex is still in education - he's studying for his A-levels at the local sixth form college.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's great, thank you for confirming that Alex is studying for A-levels at sixth form college. A-levels count as approved education, so that's a positive sign for eligibility.

Now I have a couple more questions about your circumstances:

1. Do you live in the UK?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - we're in Manchester.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you! Manchester is lovely.

Now, regarding your responsibility for Alex:

Do you live with Alex, or if not, do you contribute at least the equivalent of the Child Benefit amount (currently £25.60 per week for the eldest child) towards their upkeep (for example, on food, clothes, or pocket money)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent, thank you for confirming that.

Just a couple more questions to complete the assessment:

Does Alex currently:
- Work for 24 hours or more per week?
- Receive any benefits in their own right (such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance)?
- Have an apprenticeship?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't work - he's focused on his A-levels right now. He doesn't receive any benefits in his own name, and he's not doing an apprenticeship.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for providing all that information. I now have everything I need to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, I'm pleased to tell you that **you are eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's a summary of why you qualify:

✅ **You live in the UK** (Manchester)

✅ **You are responsible for Alex** – he lives at home with you

✅ **Alex is under 20 and in approved education** – A-levels at sixth form college qualifies as approved non-advanced education

✅ **Alex doesn't work 24+ hours per week**

✅ **Alex doesn't receive benefits in his own right**

✅ **Alex is not on an apprenticeship**

You should be able to continue receiving Child Benefit for Alex until he finishes his A-levels, or until he turns 20 – whichever comes first. If his circumstances change (for example, if he leaves education, starts working 24+ hours a week, or starts receiving benefits), you would need to inform HMRC as this could affect your eligibility.

If you haven't already claimed Child Benefit, you can make a new claim through the government website. Is there anything else you'd like to know?

All eligibility criteria are met.
